# Cognitive enhancers in healthy individuals have little benefit and significant potential harms

- Published: 27 April 2023
- Practical Issues and Updates

- Cite this article

Drugs & Therapy Perspectives Aims and scope Submit manuscript

## Abstract

Cognitive enhancers (also known as nootropics, pharmaceutical enhancers or smart drugs) are gaining in popularity among healthy individuals and workers to increase their performance and productivity. This pharmaceutical cognitive doping behaviour is fraught with issues such as minimal neuroenhancement effects, significant potential harms (e.g. addictive behaviour, paradoxical cognitive decline and severe complications) and ethical questions. Their use in healthy individuals is discouraged and raising awareness about related harms is essential.
